lines.en: Axe on my shoulder as I walk.
I head for the stem grove.
The echoes in the grove are muffled.
Step around the fallen stem.
These boots have walked ten years of groves.
Wood shavings cling to my legs.
Three big stems are due today.
My brother walks this same path.
The stem shadows sway under my feet.
I drag rope along to bind the logs.
I have walked the pale misty groves too.
Slow down; the axe edge swings.
I hone this blade every day.
I listen for the hollow in the stem.
This grain runs crooked.
Shavings fill my apron fold.
I flip the haft over and check it.
The grove drips loud in the quiet.
My brother always cuts faster than me.
This piece could make a stool.
My hands are covered in resin.
I wait for the wind to drop.
You stand too close to the stem.
Buying wood? Give me the size.
Keep your hand off the edge.
Your smell is unfamiliar to me.
I am checking whether you carry an axe.
New face; what brings you to the grove?
Can you tell my brother from me?
You stepped on my cutting mark.
I do not sell wood on credit.
Look up; do not let a stem fall on you.
The axe is still in hand; calm down.
That blow knocked me into a stem.
Sawdust got into the cut.
I bite down and stay silent.
My shoulder went numb for a moment.
I brace against the stem to stand.
Your hit is lighter than a falling stem.
The calluses on my hands saved me.
I switch the axe to my other hand.
Nobody in this grove will help me.
A golden axe? I am not used to it.
This gold could buy a fine edge.
Are you carrying a whetstone?
I smell fresh-cut wood on you.
Let me see that piece of timber.
I am not greedy; just a good axe.
One gold ingot covers two bundles.
Do not flash bright things at my eyes.
Is there a saw under your arm?
I would rather have sturdy rope.
The axe nearly slipped from my grip.
You hit the log on my shoulder.
Bark rubbed all over you.
Step aside; I carry a whole stem.
That knocked my cap crooked.
Wood dust flew off me.
Steady; do not touch my hands.
A light bump; the wood is fine.
You stand in the felling line.
Neither of us stands steady now.
My brother married before me.
She says I reek of sawdust.
Marriage needs a wooden house.
I carved her a wooden bird.
Two cutters fell twice as fast.
The little ones must not touch the axe.
I am clumsy; carving is all I know.
The wedding should be in the grove.
The sound of falling stems frightens her.
I am saving timber for a house.
Good timber; I will take it.
Whose axe wedge is this?
This branch will do as a haft.
I shake the chips into my bag.
A piece of gold for the chest.
This rope still has some use.
There is a lump of resin here.
Picking things up is a piglin's nature.
A splinter is stuck in my finger.
I am keeping this piece aside.
The sounds in the grove are wrong.
Who is cutting my marked stem?
Someone has shifted my timber pile.
That shape flickers between the stems.
It snapped my measuring rod.
That stem is falling the wrong way.
I move the axe to my right hand.
Something is gnawing at the bark.
I blow one short note first.
Keep it out of the cutting ground.
I know this grove; it does not.
It is heading toward my brother.
I drop the rope and walk over.
My grip is already set.
I follow it through the stem shadows.
It thinks the stems hide it.
I circle halfway around the timber pile.
The axe edge stays angled at it.
Each inch it retreats, I advance.
I clear the logs at the junction.
Its steps snap the dry branches.
I can hear it breathing.
Do not back under the leaning stem.
I crouch and wait for it closer.
This grove has just one way out.
It stopped, and so did I.
I swing at the air behind it.
A good cutter reads the wind.
The axe's flat hits its chest.
I swing wide, keeping the edge back.
That blow carried my felling strength.
It hits a stem; the stem shakes.
I jab my haft at its jaw.
Sawdust flies with the axe wind.
I chop down; it twists aside.
The haft has raised a blister.
I go for its knee this time.
Do not make me turn the edge.

lines.zh: 这是砍了十年树的力气。
lines.en: Ten years of felling gave me this.
I fall back behind the logs.
It grabbed my apron and tore it.
After this, the axe needs honing.
Dawn comes; mist still hangs in the grove.
I hone the axe before leaving.

lines.zh: 今天轮到我去东边林子。
lines.en: Today I take the eastern grove.
Two stems came down last night.
Rope on my shoulder; off I go.
My brother's axe rings over there.
Vines have blocked the grove path.
This stretch is mine to cut.
First I check which way it leans.
The village needs timber for roofs.
Still wearing the split gloves.
I stand on a stump and listen.
Sparks bit the back of my neck.
I slid down off the stem.
Why is there so much water here?
The blast silenced the whole grove.
An arrow sticks in the stump.
Something wraps me like roots.
Cutting hungry makes my hands shake.
Lightning split the crimson stem.
Falling, with nothing left to grab.
